works.title: Iberia (suite for piano, 12 pieces in 4 books)

position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: Spanish nationalist piano / late-Romantic harmony × cante jondo and Andalusian folk material
position_in_era.historical_role: Founding figure of Spanish musical nationalism. *Iberia* (1905–09), a 12-piece programmatic suite, paints Spanish regional portraits using cante-jondo melisma, flamenco rhythmic cells and Andalusian folk material processed through late-Romantic / proto-Impressionist harmonic vocabulary. Together with Falla, Granados and Turina, Albéniz constitutes the precedent layer that flamenco-piano historiography (cf. Trancoso's thesis hosted by the Lebrija municipal archive) names as the classical antecedent of the flamenco-piano tradition Dorantes belongs to. Dorantes himself, in his RomArchive portrait, describes 'reaching into the late romanticist harmony of Falla, Granados, and Albéniz' for harmonic and compositional vocabulary.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Iberia composed 1905–1909, published in 4 books. Premiered piecemeal in Paris by Blanche Selva. Considered Albéniz's masterwork and one of the most technically demanding solo-piano works of the early 20th century.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Albéniz introduced Falla and Joaquín Turina to Parisian musical circles, directly shaping their aesthetic. The mentorship triangle Albéniz → Falla / Turina (and adjacent: Granados) formed the core of Spanish musical nationalism c. 1900–1925.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Paris (composition + premiere) and Madrid; the Iberia material itself maps onto Andalusian / Castilian / Catalan locales — the suite is itself a cartography of Spain.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Solo piano. The harmonic language fuses post-Wagnerian chromaticism, Debussian whole-tone and modal colours, with cante-jondo melismatic figuration and zapateado rhythmic figures.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Posthumous editions and continued recording history; *Iberia* canonical in 20th-century piano repertoire and explicitly cited in flamenco-piano genealogies (Trancoso 2011 thesis 'El piano flamenco: génesis, recorrido diacrónico y análisis musicológico').
